title: Docker & Kubernetes
subtitle: Package applications in containers, run them on Kubernetes and deliver them with GitOps
audience_line: Developers, system administrators and DevOps engineers starting with containers
overview: This programme takes participants from their first container to a multi-service application running on Kubernetes and delivered by GitOps. They build small, secure images, run multi-container applications with Docker Compose, then deploy them on Kubernetes: workloads, services and network policies, configuration and storage, traffic routing with the Gateway API and TLS, autoscaling, Helm charts, monitoring, security and an overview of managed clusters on EKS and AKS. The last phase introduces GitOps with Argo CD and per-environment configuration with Kustomize and Helm. The same application is carried through every phase, and the programme closes with a final project in which teams containerise, deploy and present a multi-service application.

facts.label: Audience
facts.value: Developers, system administrators and DevOps engineers starting with containers

facts.label: Prerequisites
facts.value: Linux command line (course: Linux & Bash Scripting, or equivalent). No prior container experience needed

facts.label: Duration
facts.value: 57 h: 48 h of chapters + 9 h buffer

facts.label: Format
facts.value: Short lectures followed by guided labs; one application carried through every phase

facts.label: Lab environment
facts.value: Runs locally: one laptop per participant (16 GB RAM minimum, Docker, kind, kubectl, Helm, VS Code) and a GitHub repository per team for GitOps; managed clusters (EKS, AKS) shown by trainer demonstration; no cloud account or cost for participants

facts.label: Assessment
facts.value: A lab validated at the end of each phase and a final project presented to the group; certificate of completion for participants who complete both

facts.label: Outcome
facts.value: Participants can containerise a multi-service application, deploy it on Kubernetes with Helm, routing, TLS, autoscaling and monitoring, and deliver it from Git with Argo CD

phases.name: Docker
phases.focus: Images, containers, storage, networking, Compose and security
phases.intro: Participants learn what a container really is, then build and run them: efficient multi-stage images, persistent storage, container networking and multi-container applications with Docker Compose, with security scanning and the practices that keep containers easy to operate. Validated lab: the course application (frontend, API and database) running with Docker Compose from small, non-root images that pass a Trivy scan.

chapters.title: Containers vs VMs
chapters.content: Namespaces, cgroups, OCI, Docker Engine, containerd

chapters.title: Running Containers
chapters.content: run, ps, exec and logs, ports, environment variables, restart policies, resource limits

chapters.title: Building Images
chapters.content: Dockerfile, layers and cache, CMD vs ENTRYPOINT, multi-stage builds, image size

chapters.title: Storage
chapters.content: Volumes, bind mounts, tmpfs, backup and restore

chapters.title: Networking
chapters.content: Bridge, host and overlay networks, DNS between containers

chapters.title: Docker Compose
chapters.content: Services, health checks, env files, profiles, development and production overrides

chapters.title: Security & Registries
chapters.content: Trivy scanning, non-root users, read-only filesystems, private registry

chapters.title: Best Practices
chapters.content: Twelve-factor apps, logging, sidecar pattern, debugging containers

phases.name: Kubernetes
phases.focus: Workloads, services, configuration, storage, routing, scaling, Helm, security
phases.intro: Participants move the course application from Compose to a local Kubernetes cluster and learn each object it needs: workloads, services and network policies, configuration and secrets, persistent storage, traffic routing with the Gateway API and TLS from cert-manager, resource limits and autoscaling, Helm packaging, monitoring with Prometheus and Grafana, and basic security. Ingress is covered for existing clusters, including migration away from the retired ingress-nginx. Validated lab: the course application installed from a Helm chart, reachable over HTTPS through the Gateway API and scaled by the Horizontal Pod Autoscaler.

chapters.title: Architecture
chapters.content: Control plane, nodes, kubectl, local clusters (kind, minikube)

chapters.title: Pods & Deployments
chapters.content: Pods, ReplicaSets, Deployments, rolling updates

chapters.title: Other Workloads
chapters.content: DaemonSets, StatefulSets, Jobs, CronJobs

chapters.title: Services & Networking
chapters.content: ClusterIP, NodePort, LoadBalancer, CoreDNS, NetworkPolicies

chapters.title: Configuration
chapters.content: ConfigMaps, Secrets

chapters.title: Storage
chapters.content: PersistentVolumes, PersistentVolumeClaims, StorageClasses

chapters.title: Traffic Routing
chapters.content: Gateway API, Ingress (ingress-nginx retired in March 2026) and migration, TLS with cert-manager

chapters.title: Scaling
chapters.content: Requests and limits, resource quotas, Horizontal Pod Autoscaler

chapters.title: Helm
chapters.content: Charts, values, install, upgrade and rollback

chapters.title: Observability & Troubleshooting
chapters.content: describe, logs and events, metrics-server, Prometheus and Grafana installed with Helm

chapters.title: Security Basics
chapters.content: RBAC, ServiceAccounts, Pod Security Standards

chapters.title: Managed Kubernetes
chapters.content: Amazon EKS and Azure AKS overview, trainer demonstration

phases.name: GitOps
phases.focus: Argo CD, the pull model, environments with Kustomize and Helm
phases.intro: With GitOps, the cluster pulls its desired state from Git instead of receiving commands. Participants install Argo CD, deliver the course application from a Git repository, roll back by reverting a commit, and manage development and production environments with Kustomize overlays and Helm values. Validated lab: a change merged in Git that reaches the development environment automatically and production after promotion.

chapters.title: GitOps & Argo CD
chapters.content: Principles, pull model, Argo CD installation

chapters.title: Argo CD in Practice
chapters.content: Applications, sync, rollback, app-of-apps

chapters.title: Environments
chapters.content: Kustomize overlays, Helm values per environment

phases.name: Final Project
phases.focus: A multi-service application, from Compose to GitOps
phases.intro: Teams of two or three containerise and deploy a provided multi-service application, reusing the phase labs, then present it as they would to an engineering team.

chapters.title: Brief & Build
chapters.content: Read the brief, containerise the frontend, API and database, write the Compose file for development and the Helm chart

chapters.title: Deliver & Document
chapters.content: Gateway API routing with TLS, autoscaling, monitoring, delivery by Argo CD; README and architecture diagram

chapters.title: Demo & Review
chapters.content: Live demo of a change delivered from Git, then a rollback; questions and feedback

project.title: A Multi-Service Application on Kubernetes
project.brief: A frontend, an API and a database containerised, run with Compose for development, packaged as a Helm chart, routed over HTTPS through the Gateway API, autoscaled and monitored, and delivered to the cluster by Argo CD from Git.
project.stack: Docker, Docker Compose, Trivy, Kubernetes (kind), Helm, Gateway API, cert-manager, Prometheus, Grafana, Argo CD, Kustomize, Git
project.deliverable: Git repository with Dockerfiles, Compose file, Helm chart and Argo CD manifests, architecture diagram, live demo
